title: Parallel Simulation of Josephson Junctions With Multiplicative Noise
authors: Vincenzo Pierro, Luigi Troiano, Elena Mejuto Villa, Sergio Pagano, Giovanni Filatrella
abstract: Parallel graphic processing units have been employed for fast simulations of the switching dynam- ics of Josephson junctions subject to critical current fluctuations. Such a system is modeled by a nonequilibrium washboard model with multiplicative noise, for which analytical results are lacking. The proposed approach allows us to execute extensive numerical simulation in short time and with relatively inexpensive resources. This allows us to fully characterize the effect of the noise on the junction switching current distributions at realistic bias current sweeprates.
summary: This work develops a GPU-accelerated numerical technique to simulate the switching dynamics of Josephson junctions under multiplicative noise. By simulating the system's response to varying bias sweep rates and noise levels, the authors characterize how noise fundamentally alters the switching current distribution. This methodology is crucial for understanding noise effects in superconducting quantum devices.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of fast and accurate simulation of Josephson junction switching dynamics when subjected to multiplicative noise, for which analytical solutions are unavailable.
main_result: GPU acceleration significantly speeds up simulations, allowing characterization of how multiplicative noise affects the switching current distribution, showing dependencies on both noise intensity and bias sweep rate.
method: The authors employed numerical simulation using the Euler-Maruyama method, parallelized across Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) via CUDA to handle extensive bias sweep rate variations.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Josephson Junction (JJ) modeled by a nonequilibrium washboard potential. The dynamics are governed by a stochastic differential equation incorporating multiplicative noise arising from fluctuations in the critical current.
key_observables: The primary observables are the switching current distribution (characterized by median and width) and the comparison of the derived equivalent temperature ($T_{	ext{fit}}$) under different noise regimes.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the noise amplitude ($\Sigma$), the bias sweep velocity ($v_\gamma$), and the junction parameters ($R, C,  ar{I}_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes Gaussian fluctuations for the critical current and utilizes the Euler-Maruyama method for numerical integration.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares the Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) of switching currents for noisy vs. non-noisy cases. Figure 3 shows how the PDF shifts with increasing bias sweep velocity ($v_\gamma$), and Figure 4 shows the effect of noise intensity ($\Sigma$) on the PDF.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model and governing equations, details the GPU-accelerated numerical simulation approach, presents results analyzing the effect of noise and sweep rate on the switching current distribution, and concludes by discussing the implications for noise modeling in superconducting devices.
why_interesting: The study provides a powerful, scalable numerical framework for analyzing non-equilibrium dynamics in superconducting circuits, which are central to quantum computing architectures. The comparison of noise effects across different rates is highly relevant for understanding decoherence mechanisms.
